_comment: Demo catalog for DemoBrowser.lua. Order = browsing order (PgDn/PgUp). 'category' groups the demos in the list; demos with the same category must be together. The files, scripts and shaders shown in the info panel are read from each scene JSON, not from here. "tour" = scene names of the showcase playlist the browser starts with (Prev/Next walk it in this order; the Tour/All button or F3 switches to the full list).

demos.title: Hello world
demos.summary: The smallest script: it writes a message, the run time and the FPS on the screen every frame. Start here.
learn: Global script: onStart() once, onUpdate() every frame, onEnd() when it stops

demos.title: Keyboard and mouse
demos.summary: Reads the keyboard and the mouse and shows on screen what the engine sees: keys held, keys just pressed and the mouse position and buttons.
controls: W A S D, Space, E   hold them and watch the panel
learn: Components:Input(): isCharPressed (held) and isCharFirstEventDown (only the first frame)

demos.title: Moving an object
demos.summary: Moves the cube in different ways: along the world axes, up and down, along its own forward direction and rotating on the spot. It is an object script: the same script can be attached to any object.
controls: W A S D   move on the floor
I / K   forward / back along the object's own axis
learn: Object script: 'this' is the object the script is attached to
Speeds: speed in units/s, rotationSpeed in degrees/s (rotation matrices take degrees, not radians)

demos.title: Rotating an object
demos.summary: Three ways of rotating: around each axis with the keys, automatically every frame, and resetting to the starting rotation.
learn: M3 rotation matrices: setMatrixRotationForEulerAngles and multiplying matrices
Angles are in degrees: rotationSpeed is degrees/s (90 = a quarter turn per second); auto-rotation turns 45 degrees/s

demos.title: Creating and removing objects
demos.summary: Creates coloured point lights at random places from a script, hides them and removes them again. The lights are invisible objects: you see them as pools of colour on the floor and the cubes. The panel counts them (the script stops at 32; the engine supports 64 point lights in total).
controls: C   create a random coloured light
V   show / hide the last one
learn: ObjectFactory.LightPoint creates the object and adds it to the scene by itself (do not call AddObject3D again)
object:setEnabled(false) hides it, object:setRemoved(true) removes it

demos.title: Parenting (hierarchies)
demos.summary: Parent and children: four coloured point lights are attached to the cube. When the cube moves or turns they go with it, and their offsets can be animated or detached. The children are lights, so you see them as coloured light on the floor.
controls: W A S D   move the parent
I   print info to the console
learn: Children keep their position relative to the parent

demos.title: Look at a target
demos.summary: The cone turns to face a sphere that circles around it. Instantly or smoothly, and you can switch the following off and turn it by hand.
controls: A / D   turn by hand (follow off)
learn: Finding the target by name with Brakeza:getObjectByName
Dot product to know whether the object already faces the target

demos.title: A camera that follows
demos.summary: The camera follows the cube smoothly from behind. The cube is moved with the Movement lesson's keys. Shows how to take the camera away from the keyboard.
controls: W A S D   move the cube
learn: Components:Input():setKeyboardEnabled(false) so the keys do not also move the camera
camera:setPosition with a lerp towards a point behind the object, and camera:LookAt(object)

demos.title: Variables of another object
demos.summary: One cube holds two script variables (offset and count, which grows every second). The sphere reads them every second and prints them to the Logs / Console window.
controls: Open the Logs / Console window to see the values
learn: object:getLocalScriptVar(name) reads a variable of another object's script
Variables are declared in the script's .json file

demos.title: Lights
demos.summary: Creates a point light from a script and lets you move it, rotate the sun and change the ambient light while it runs.
controls: Z / X   less / more ambient light
I K J L   move the point light
learn: ObjectFactory.LightPoint and its attenuation (setConstant / setLinear / setCuadratic)
Global illumination from Lua through Components:Render()

demos.title: Physics (rigid bodies)
demos.summary: A box with a Bullet rigid body falls and lands on the floor. Apply forces, impulses and velocities to it, stop it or turn its physics off.
controls: W A S D   apply a force
I / K   set the velocity directly
learn: Rigid bodies: mass, friction, restitution and damping
this:onGround() only works for KINEMATIC characters: a rigid body checks the ground with a ray (isRayCollisionWith)

demos.title: Collisions and rays
demos.summary: The player box falls onto an enemy and is knocked back; touching a pickup removes it. R shoots a visible ray at the target and G checks the ground below.
controls: R   cast a ray at 'Target' (drawn 3 s: green = hit, red = miss)
G   check the ground (ray drawn downwards)

demos.title: Skeletal animation
demos.summary: A character with several skeletal animations. Switch between them, change their speed, turn looping on and off, and see them chosen automatically when you walk.
controls: 1 idle   2 walk   3 run   4 jump   5 crouch walk
W A S D   walk / idle
learn: Mesh3DAnimation: setAnimationByName needs the exact animation name stored in the FBX

demos.title: Particles from a script
demos.summary: Creates a particle emitter above the torch from code and configures it: emission rate, lifespan, gravity, speed and colours.

demos.title: Audio
demos.summary: Registers sounds and a music loop, plays them and controls their volume. Make sure your speakers are on.
controls: Q W E R T   beep, click, coin, hit, success
learn: Components:Sound(): AddSound / AddMusic register, PlaySound / PlayMusic play by label

demos.title: Updating a shader from a script
demos.summary: A post-processing shader called Custom tints the whole screen. The script writes new values into its variables every frame.

demos.title: Show room
demos.summary: A small set of meshes and lights to look at the deferred renderer: G-Buffer, ADS lighting, shadows and a chromatic aberration post-processing shader on top.
learn: Post-processing shader stored in the scene shaders list

demos.title: Lights and day/night cycle
demos.summary: Point and spot lights plus a global (directional) light that a scene script rotates to simulate a 30 s day/night cycle, changing ambient and diffuse colours over time.

demos.title: Post-processing chain
demos.summary: Eight full-screen shaders chained one after another, each changing a different cell of a 4x2 grid on the screen. Switch each one on and off with the number keys and watch how the ping-pong buffers pass the image from one shader to the next.
controls: 1 - 8      toggle that shader (the key follows the grid: 1 2 3 4 on the top row, 5 6 7 8 on the bottom)
learn: Scene shaders run after the light pass (frame step 6)
UVs are screen space: gl_FragCoord.xy / textureSize
Shader node editor and code editor in the editor GUI

demos.title: Node shaders showcase
demos.summary: Fourteen objects, each wearing a different node shader (hologram, lava, burning dissolve, toon outline, rim light, scanner...) and twelve full-screen node effects (sepia, night vision, thermal, chromatic aberration, underwater, ripple...) that the script switches on one at a time. All of them are node graphs you can open and edit in the shader node editor.
controls: Left / Right  previous / next screen effect
Space         automatic effect change on / off
R             spin the objects / keep them still
H             show / hide the panel and the labels
Mouse wheel   zoom in / out (Shift = faster)
W A S D / Q E   move / go down or up
learn: Object shaders (NodeMesh3D) are listed in each mesh; screen shaders (NodePostprocessing) in the scene shaders list
Components:Render():getSceneShaderByLabel(name) also returns node shaders: shader:setEnabled / isEnabled
Examples in assets/shaders/Examples/NodeMesh3D and NodePostprocessing: open them with the shaders window

demos.title: Particle emitters
demos.summary: Thirty particle emitters on a carousel that rotates in front of the camera, one effect at a time. Fire, smoke, sparks, water and weather, plus the newer controls: spiral and vortex motion (helix, tornado, galaxy, sprinkler, black hole), emission shapes (sphere, torus, cone, the surface of a chess pawn) and effects such as a portal, lightning, bubbles, fireworks and confetti. Each effect gets its own background colour and zoom so it can be seen well; lightning and fireworks fire in bursts. Every emitter is configured from the editor and saved in the scene.
controls: M           automatic view (background colour and zoom per effect) on / off
learn: Scene script: ParticleCarousel.lua (moves the emitters in a circle)
Emitter settings are part of the object JSON
ParticlesContext SWIRL_* / SPIRAL_*: curved paths around the emitter axis (examples 17-20)
Object Properties window (F10 in the editor) to tweak them live
ParticleCarousel.lua: window:setClearColor for the background, emitter:setStopAdd for bursts, camera dolly for the zoom
ParticlesContext: SHAPE_*, SWIRL_* and SPIRAL_* (see the inspector section of each emitter)

demos.title: Swarm (boids)
demos.summary: A Swarm object steering thirty meshes with the classic boids rules: separation, alignment and cohesion. The members are ordinary meshes referenced by the swarm. The red cube is the swarm's predator: the boids steer away from it, and panic (run faster than normal) when it gets close. You choose how the predator moves.
controls: 1 / 2 / 3  figure-eight / hunt nearest boid / parked in the centre
learn: Swarm members are resolved after loading and retried every 0.25 s until all exist

demos.title: Rain of physics cubes
demos.summary: Three emitter objects run an object script that spawns a physics cube every half second. The cubes are Bullet rigid bodies that fall and pile up on the floor. Only the newest 30 cubes of each emitter are kept so the physics world does not grow forever.
learn: Object script: RainCubesDemo.lua (this is the owner object)
Script variables (frequency) come from the JSON types file of the script

demos.title: Projectiles and collisions
demos.summary: A launcher fires physics projectiles; an object script logs on screen every collision it receives.
controls: Mouse   hold the right button and move to aim
Q / E   less / more power (or the mouse wheel)

demos.title: First person (starter kit)
demos.summary: A kinematic capsule with a first-person camera: walk, jump and look around a small test level. The controller is an ordinary object script attached to the capsule, so it can be copied to your own character.
controls: Hold the left mouse button and drag to look around
Tab        free look: the mouse is captured and you look around without pressing anything (Tab or Esc release it)
learn: Kinematic body mode (character): gravity, onGround(), no rigid-body push-back
The script drives the camera from the capsule position every frame

demos.title: Third person (starter kit)
demos.summary: A kinematic capsule with a camera that follows it from behind and always looks at it. Dragging the mouse turns the character and the camera around it. The controller is an ordinary object script attached to the capsule, so it can be copied to your own character.
controls: W A S D     move (relative to where the character faces)
Hold the left mouse button and drag sideways to turn
learn: Kinematic body mode (character): setWalkingDirection, jump, onGround
Follow camera: position from the character's rotation, camera:LookAt(point), smoothed with an exponential factor

demos.title: 2D platformer (starter kit)
demos.summary: Side-scrolling platformer in a 3D level. The player is a ghost collider moved by script, without Bullet rigid bodies: raycasts for the floor and walls give coyote time, jump buffering, variable jump height and wall sliding.
controls: Space       jump (hold for a higher jump)
W / S       up / down (S while falling drops faster)
learn: Ghost body mode (trigger) used as a character controller
Floor and wall detection with raycasts instead of physics contacts

demos.title: Twin-stick shooter (starter kit)
demos.summary: Top-down shooter with twin-stick controls: one stick moves, the other one aims. It also plays with keyboard and mouse. Shoot the eight targets, dash, reload; they come back after a few seconds. The script converts screen directions to the world with the camera, so any fixed top-down camera works.
controls: GAMEPAD   left stick move, right stick aim, RT or RB shoot, LT or A dash, X reload
KEYBOARD  W A S D move, mouse aim, left button shoot, right button dash, R reload
The HUD shows the scheme you used last
learn: Camera:worldToScreenXYZ to turn a screen direction into a world direction (works for any fixed camera)
Rigid body moved with setLinearVelocity; bullets are plain meshes moved by the script and checked by distance

demos.title: UI widgets
demos.summary: The JSON widget system: a nested widget, a list widget and single cards drawn at a position, all fed with data from Lua every frame.

demos.title: Text rendering
demos.summary: Every way of drawing text: TTF auto-size, TTF with explicit size, batched glyph atlas, centred and aligned text, and cached text.
learn: Atlas text is the cheapest for HUDs that change every frame

demos.title: Mouse cursor
demos.summary: The mouse cursor changes with the object under it: select, attack, acquire and move cursors over four different targets and the floor. The same pattern drives the cursor in the RTS: ask the engine what is under the mouse (asynchronous picking) and swap the cursor image only when the state changes.
controls: Mouse      hover the objects and the floor
learn: The same pattern in the RTS: assets/scripts/RTS/Systems/CursorManager.lua

demos.title: Multi-selection
demos.summary: Twelve selectable objects on a floor. Selected objects get an orange outline, a pulsing ring on the floor and an order number; a group also shows its centre, lines to every member and a ring around them all. Click one to select it, Ctrl+click to add or remove objects from the group, or Ctrl+drag a rectangle to select several at once. The panel lists the group and its positions, and the keyboard moves the whole group together.
controls: Ctrl + click    add / remove an object from the group
W A S D Q Z     move the whole group (Q up, Z down)
X               remove the last object from the group
P               print a report of the group to the console
learn: How selected objects are drawn: object:setHighlight (engine outline), drawGroundCircle rings, camera:worldToScreenXYZ labels, DrawLine to the group centre
object:addToPosition to move every object in the group

demos.title: Positional sound (Sound3D)
demos.summary: Four looping sound sources placed in the scene, three fixed and one orbiting the centre. The camera is the listener: volume falls off in a straight line between each source's inner radius (full volume) and outer radius (silence), and with panning on the sound moves to the left or right speaker depending on where the source is. The panel shows distance, volume and pan of every source; the rings on the floor show the two radii.
controls: R           show / hide the radius rings
learn: src/3D/Sound3D.cpp: linear distance volume and left/right panning
Sound3D objects can also be saved in a scene and edited in the inspector (debugDraw shows the rings)

demos.title: Video player
demos.summary: Plays an MP4 from a script in two formats: full screen, or in a plane (a framed window that covers only part of the screen, with the scene visible around it and a progress bar). You can switch between them while it plays. When the video ends the torus jumps to one side (and back on the next play); skipping it does not count as finishing it. This is the pattern the RTS uses for its intro video.
controls: V          play full screen (restarts it if it is playing)
B          play in the plane / window (restarts it if it is playing)
F          switch between full screen and plane while it plays
Any other key or click   skip the video
learn: image:setSize(w, h): size as a fraction of the screen (1.0 = full screen); image:setScreenPosition(x, y) in pixels
The plane keeps the 16:9 shape of the video by using the real window aspect ratio
ObjectFactory.PlayVideoCutscene(path, fadeOut) for a blocking cutscene
The same pattern in the RTS intro: assets/scripts/RTS/Systems/MenuManager.lua

demos.title: Performance test
demos.summary: Spawns objects in batches to stress the engine: static meshes, physics bodies, particle emitters, point lights or animated meshes, with an FPS readout.
controls: Left/Right  spawn rate      M / N  object cap
learn: ObjectFactory.* to create objects from Lua
Profiler window in the editor to see where the frame goes
